newsitem.title: USA: U.S. regrets unionist vote on disarming guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. regrets unionist vote on disarming guerrillas.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said on Wednesday Washington regretted a vote by Northern Ireland unionist parties against Anglo-Irish proposals for disarming guerrillas in the British-ruled province.
"We regret that vote," spokesman James Foley told reporters. "I think the important point, though, is that the process will continue," he said.
"The British and Irish governments have expressed commitment to this process leading to a negotiated settlement. We don't see this vote as an end of that process," Foley said.

Wednesday's vote by the three unionist parties, which want Northern Ireland to remain linked to Britain, defeated proposals that Irish Republican Army guerrillas fighting for a united Ireland and pro-British guerrilla groups should disarm while taking part in peace talks.

Shortly afterwards the American chairman of the talks, former Sen. George Mitchell, announced that the multi-party negotiations to end three decades of violence in Northern Ireland would adjourn next Monday until September.
"We hope very much that this process will produce what the people of Northern Ireland want -- peace, political stability and reconciliation," Mitchell said.
The Irish Republican Army called a ceasefire at the weekend which will admit its political wing, Sinn Fein, to the talks in September if Britain deems the truce genuine.
